data.narrative:
Corvex Systems is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jason Blick that has raised $5M+. The valuation assessment draws from a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable (277810.KQ), including peers such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using the $5M total raised as a proxy for baseline value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $12M. A peer-median comparison cannot be reliably constructed due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the robotics sector—only one same-stage peer and one adjacent-stage peer were identified, falling short of the three-datapoint minimum needed for statistical validity. Expanding to the full 11-company robotics peer set would introduce uncontrolled stage and scale heterogeneity.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $11M to $14M, with a median estimate of $12M. This range reflects a moderate band around the stage-progression output. Key uncertainties include the absence of tightly-filtered peer comparables, which prevents cross-validation of the stage-based multiple, and limited visibility into Corvex's current revenue or unit economics relative to the identified peer set. Any material update to product-market fit metrics or capital efficiency would warrant reassessment.
